openQuestions.q: decision_set option A accepts generated-token for critic/exclusion-approver signing. owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md line 267 says generated-token fallback is preferable to ppid when both identity dimensions are validated, and line 288-290 says the ppid fallback specifically is intentionally weaker and not acceptable as a review-independence anchor. On a close read this weakness statement is scoped to ppid (the subsection it appears in), not generated-token, so the doc does not appear to forbid generated-token for review independence. But no passage in the doc explicitly blesses generated-token FOR the review-independence property either -- every generated-token passage is written in the general write-coordination/owner-lease frame. Is CHK-005 accepting generated-token as evidence of review independence (not just of write-coordination identity) consistent with this doc's intent, or does that require a documented decision that generated-token is sufficient specifically for the independence property this story exists to protect?
openQuestions.evidence: owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:267-270 Generated-token fallback is preferable to ppid fallback when the host adapter can define and preserve both durable identity dimensions; owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:288-290 This fallback is intentionally weaker. It is acceptable for local accidental coordination because stale-lease takeover exists; it is not acceptable as a review-independence or Authority-proof anchor.
openQuestions.resolution: Accept generated-token for the review-independence property. The disqualifying sentence at owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:288-290 ("This fallback is intentionally weaker... not acceptable as a review-independence or Authority-proof anchor") sits under the "## ppid Degraded Fallback" heading at line 292s preceding section, so "this fallback" is ppid, not generated-token. The doc therefore disqualifies exactly one source from the review-independence anchor role, and it is the one this story also refuses. The generated-token passage at :267-270 conditions generation on the host defining and preserving BOTH durable identity dimensions and calls generation unsafe when either the task or agent/role boundary cannot be validated; code matches this, since owner-session-adapters.ts:160-173 gates generated-token behind the same provider plus task plus agent resolution as host-adapter and additionally requires a boundary token. So generated-token is host-derived and unmintable by an implementer on the same terms as host-adapter, which is the property this story depends on. The doc is silent rather than permissive about generated-token specifically for review-independence, and I am resolving that silence toward acceptance on the structural evidence above rather than on absence of prohibition. If a REVIEW reviewer reads the silence the other way, CHK-005 is the item to narrow, and narrowing it would cost only the generated-token acceptance while leaving the guard intact.
